the study of the immunopathogenesis of testicular inflammation.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IL-10 is a proinflammatory cytokine that can be up-regulated in the testis during autoimmune orchitis.
IL-10 is a pro-inflammatory cytokine, which is capable of enhancing the development of autoimmune testicular inflammation in vivo.
IL-10 is a pleiotropic cytokine, which can exert anti- as well as proinflammatory effects in vivo, depending on the experimental conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IL-10 is not a good candidate for the treatment of EAO.
the pro- and antiinflammatory effects of IL-10 are context dependent.
IL-10 has a dual role in autoimmune diseases, i.e., both anti- and proinflammatory, depending on the dose and time of administration, and the stage and type of disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IL-10 is a double-edged sword, capable of exerting anti-inflammatory as well as pro-inflammatory effects in the testis.
the immune response to the testis is not simply a matter of T cell activation and effector function.
IL-10 has proinflammatory effects in vivo, and this is not limited to EAO but also occurs in other experimental autoimmune models.
